When these theme parks opened.Disneyland: Walt Disney's Anaheim park opened 17 July 1955. Press day was so chaotic, with counterfeit tickets, that staff called it Black Sunday.
When these theme parks opened.Six Flags Over Texas: The name counts the six flags that have flown over Texas, and the park's success inspired a whole chain across America.
When these theme parks opened.Universal Studios Hollywood: It began as a backlot studio tour for visitors and still operates as a working film studio beside the rides.
When these theme parks opened.LEGOLAND Billund: It sits beside the Danish town where LEGO began, and its Miniland recreates world landmarks from millions of bricks.
When these theme parks opened.Walt Disney World: Its roughly 25,000 acres are bigger than the island of Manhattan, which let Disney build hotels and parks that never meet.
When these theme parks opened.Tokyo Disneyland: The first Disney park outside the US is run by the Oriental Land Company under licence and is among the world's most visited.
When these theme parks opened.Disneyland Paris: Opened as Euro Disney, it lost money early and was renamed Disneyland Paris in 1995.
When these theme parks opened.Hong Kong Disneyland: Feng shui consultants helped plan this park, and they shaped details like the angle of the entrance and placement of water.
When these theme parks opened.Shanghai Disneyland: Its Enchanted Storybook Castle is the largest of any Disney park, and the park features a Tron coaster built just for it.
When these theme parks opened.Super Nintendo World: It opened at Universal Studios Japan, and visitors play a Mario Kart ride using AR headsets and collect coins on a wristband.

When humans first settled these places.Australia: Aboriginal Australians' history there goes back at least 50,000 years, making theirs among the oldest continuous cultures on Earth.
When humans first settled these places.The Americas: Chile's Monte Verde site shows people there about 14,500 years ago, and fossil footprints at White Sands may suggest even earlier arrivals.
When humans first settled these places.Ireland: Hunter-gatherers arrived after the ice retreated, and Mount Sandel in County Derry is among the oldest known sites.
When humans first settled these places.Malta: Malta's temples, like Ġgantija, came later and are among the world's oldest freestanding stone buildings.
When humans first settled these places.Fiji: Lapita seafarers carried distinctive pottery across the Pacific and reached Fiji, ancestors of many Pacific islanders.
When humans first settled these places.Iceland: Ingólfr Arnarson founded Reykjavík, whose name means 'smoky bay' because of steam from hot springs he saw.
When humans first settled these places.Easter Island: Polynesian settlers called the island Rapa Nui and carved nearly 900 giant moai statues from volcanic rock.
When humans first settled these places.New Zealand: Māori ancestors arrived by canoe from eastern Polynesia, making New Zealand one of the last large lands settled.
When humans first settled these places.Madeira: Portuguese explorers claimed it around 1419 and its name means 'wood' for its forests. It's now famous for fortified wine.
When humans first settled these places.Cape Verde: It was uninhabited when the Portuguese arrived, and later became a hub in the Atlantic slave trade, leaving a Creole culture.

Famous numbers in computing.Max letters in a DOS file name: This is the famous 8.3 rule: eight characters plus a three-letter extension, which is why old files looked like README.TXT.
Famous numbers in computing.ASCII code of capital A: A is 65 and lowercase a is 97, exactly 32 apart, so flipping one bit changes a letter's case.
Famous numbers in computing.Classic Windows screen DPI: Windows picked it as a standard so on-screen text would scale predictably, while early Macs used 72.
Famous numbers in computing.Characters in standard ASCII: ASCII uses seven bits, giving 128 codes, and 33 of them are invisible control codes like newline.
Famous numbers in computing.Original tweet length limit: The cap came from SMS's 160 characters, minus room for a username. Twitter raised it to 280 in 2017.
Famous numbers in computing.SMS character limit: Engineer Friedhelm Hillebrand set it after counting that most postcards and telex messages ran shorter than that.
Famous numbers in computing.Largest value in one byte: An 8-bit byte holds 0 to 255, which is why web colour values run from 00 to FF in hex.
Famous numbers in computing.Bytes in a kibibyte: It's 2 to the 10th power. The name 'kibibyte' was created in 1998 to separate it from the 1,000-byte kilobyte.
Famous numbers in computing.Highest TCP port number: It's 2 to the 16th minus 1, because ports use 16 bits. The famous ports, like 80 for web traffic, sit below 1,024.
Famous numbers in computing.Max signed 32-bit integer: This is why a 'Year 2038 problem' exists: 32-bit Unix time overflows on 19 January 2038.

Levels of biological organization.Atom: The name means 'uncuttable' in Greek, yet atoms do split, and nearly all of an atom's volume is empty space around a tiny nucleus.
Levels of biological organization.Molecule: Water's bent shape, with both hydrogens on one side, gives it a slight electric charge and is why it dissolves so many substances.
Levels of biological organization.Organelle: The word means 'little organ'. Mitochondria even carry their own DNA, a relic of bacteria engulfed by early cells over a billion years ago.
Levels of biological organization.Cell: Robert Hooke coined the word in 1665 after seeing cork under a microscope; the tiny box-like chambers reminded him of monks' cells.
Levels of biological organization.Tissue: Humans have four basic types: epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous. Even blood, fat and bone count as connective tissue.
Levels of biological organization.Organ: The skin is the body's largest organ, covering about 2 square metres in an adult and weighing roughly 4 kg.
Levels of biological organization.Organ system: A human body runs about eleven of these, such as circulatory and digestive, and none works alone: the heart relies on lungs and kidneys too.
Levels of biological organization.Organism: A single organism can be one cell or trillions; a human carries roughly 30 trillion of its own cells plus a similar number of resident microbes.
Levels of biological organization.Population: Ecologists track births, deaths and migration to tell whether one of these is growing or shrinking, as with wolves reintroduced to Yellowstone.
Levels of biological organization.Community: All the interacting species in one place, such as a pond's plants, insects and fungi. Losing one keystone species can reshape the whole thing.

Units of length.Millimetre: Milli comes from the Latin mille for thousand, and a pinhead is about one to two millimetres across.
Units of length.Centimetre: The centimetre was part of the CGS system of units, and it is about the width of a fingernail.
Units of length.Inch: It has been defined as exactly 2.54 cm since the 1959 international agreement.
Units of length.Foot: It was defined with the inch in 1959, though it once varied widely by country.
Units of length.Yard: A legend says it was the length of King Henry I's arm, though that is probably only a tale.
Units of length.Metre: Originally defined as one ten-millionth of the distance from the pole to the equator, it is now defined by the speed of light.
Units of length.Kilometre: France introduced it in the 1790s; kilo comes from the Greek for thousand.
Units of length.Mile: The word comes from the Latin mille passus, a thousand paces of Roman legions.
Units of length.Nautical mile: Equal to one minute of latitude, which is why navigators use it.
Units of length.Marathon: It is 26 miles 385 yards, and the extra distance was fixed at the 1908 London Olympics, reputedly to reach the royal box.

Top speed: snail to planet.Garden snail: A snail's rasping tongue, the radula, carries thousands of microscopic teeth.
Top speed: snail to planet.Human walking: About 5 km/h is typical for people, and we naturally choose a speed that saves the most energy.
Top speed: snail to planet.Usain Bolt at full tilt: His 100 m record of 9.58 seconds in 2009 still stands, and his top speed has been clocked at about 44 km/h.
Top speed: snail to planet.Cheetah: It can go from standing to 100 km/h in about three seconds, but only for short bursts.
Top speed: snail to planet.Peregrine falcon in a dive: It is the fastest animal on Earth, and its dive, called a stoop, is how it hunts other birds.
Top speed: snail to planet.Cruising airliner: It flies around 11,000 m up, where the air is thin and drag is low.
Top speed: snail to planet.Speed of sound (sea level): At sea level the speed of sound is about 1,235 km/h, and it is slower in colder air, so Mach 1 is lower at altitude.
Top speed: snail to planet.Concorde: It cruised at twice the speed of sound, and its metal skin heated up so much that it stretched by about 20 cm in flight.
Top speed: snail to planet.The ISS in orbit: It circles the Earth every 90 minutes or so, so the crew sees about 16 sunrises a day.
Top speed: snail to planet.Earth orbiting the Sun: Earth moves at around 30 km per second, so you are speeding through space even while sitting still.

Stephen King novels, by publication.Carrie: King's first published novel nearly never existed, since he threw out the draft and his wife Tabitha rescued it from the trash.
Stephen King novels, by publication.'Salem's Lot: It is a vampire novel set in a Maine town, inspired by wondering what would happen if Dracula arrived in modern America.
Stephen King novels, by publication.The Shining: The novel was inspired by a stay at the Stanley Hotel in Colorado, and King has said he disliked Kubrick's 1980 film.
Stephen King novels, by publication.The Stand: The plague nicknamed Captain Trips wipes out most of humanity, and the 1990 uncut edition restored about 400 pages.
Stephen King novels, by publication.Cujo: King has said he barely remembers writing this novel about a rabid St Bernard because of his alcoholism then.
Stephen King novels, by publication.Pet Sematary: King held it back for years, finding it too disturbing, and it was inspired by a pet cemetery near his rented house.
Stephen King novels, by publication.It: Set in Derry, Maine, it took four years to write and runs over 1,100 pages.
Stephen King novels, by publication.Misery: Annie Wilkes, an obsessed fan, holds writer Paul Sheldon captive, and Kathy Bates won an Oscar for the film.
Stephen King novels, by publication.Dolores Claiborne: The whole novel is one monologue with no chapter breaks, as a woman gives her statement to police.
Stephen King novels, by publication.Under the Dome: A small Maine town is trapped under an invisible barrier, and King first began the idea in 1976 before abandoning it for decades.

How many years after the original came t.The Empire Strikes Back: On set, David Prowse was fed a fake line, so the 'I am your father' twist stayed secret from most of the cast and crew until the premiere.
How many years after the original came t.Ghostbusters II: The sequel gave the Stay Puft Marshmallow Man a rest and sent the team up against a river of slime beneath New York, in a 1989 release.
How many years after the original came t.Terminator 2: James Cameron's follow-up took a villain from the first film and made him a protector, and its liquid-metal T-1000 was a landmark in computer effects.
How many years after the original came t.Incredibles 2: Brad Bird's 2018 sequel earned over a billion dollars, which made it one of the highest-grossing animated films ever released at the time.
How many years after the original came t.Dumb and Dumber To: The sequel came out in 2014, two decades after the Farrelly brothers' original, with Jim Carrey and Jeff Daniels back as the dim-witted pair.
How many years after the original came t.The Color of Money: Paul Newman reprised Fast Eddie Felson from The Hustler, and won his only competitive Oscar for Best Actor for the role in 1987.
How many years after the original came t.Tron: Legacy: The 2010 follow-up to the 1982 film updated its Grid with then-cutting-edge effects and a Daft Punk score, and digitally de-aged Jeff Bridges.
How many years after the original came t.Coming 2 America: Eddie Murphy returned as Prince Akeem in this 2021 follow-up, released straight to streaming after the original's 1988 hit.
How many years after the original came t.Top Gun: Maverick: The 2022 sequel to the 1986 Tom Cruise film used real fighter jets, with its actors training to endure intense g-forces in the cockpit.
How many years after the original came t.Mary Poppins Returns: Emily Blunt took the role Julie Andrews won an Oscar for, and Dick Van Dyke, then 92, danced on a desk in this 2018 film.

How a sound travels from the air to your.Pinna (outer ear): The visible, folded part of the ear funnels sound and shapes it, and its ridges help us tell whether a sound comes from above or below.
How a sound travels from the air to your.Ear canal: This canal is about 2.5 cm long and makes earwax, which traps dust and keeps the skin supple.
How a sound travels from the air to your.Eardrum: A thin membrane that vibrates with incoming sound, just about 0.1 mm thick, and it can be ruptured by a loud blast or a sharp pressure change.
How a sound travels from the air to your.Malleus (hammer): The first of the three smallest bones in the body, named for its hammer shape, and it is attached directly to the eardrum.
How a sound travels from the air to your.Incus (anvil): The middle link, shaped like a blacksmith's anvil, passes the vibrations onward from the hammer.
How a sound travels from the air to your.Stapes (stirrup): At about 3 mm long, this stirrup-shaped bone is the smallest bone in the human body.
How a sound travels from the air to your.Oval window: This membrane-covered opening to the inner ear is smaller than the eardrum, which helps amplify the vibrations before they enter fluid.
How a sound travels from the air to your.Cochlea: This snail-shaped organ's name is Greek for snail, and its fluid-filled coil holds around 15,000 hair cells that convert vibrations into nerve signals.
How a sound travels from the air to your.Auditory nerve: This bundle of about 30,000 fibers carries signals from the ear to the brainstem, and then onward in the brain.
How a sound travels from the air to your.Auditory cortex: Located in the temporal lobe, this region turns the nerve signals into recognizable sounds, such as speech and music.

Italian brands, by founding year.Campari: Its red color historically came from cochineal insects, until the company dropped them for a synthetic dye in 2006.
Italian brands, by founding year.Martini & Rossi: This Turin company built an empire on vermouth, an Italian aperitif wine flavored with herbs, and sponsors Formula 1 as Martini Racing.
Italian brands, by founding year.Pirelli: Based in Milan, it began with rubber and later tires, and is known for its annual calendar, which features famous photographers.
Italian brands, by founding year.Barilla: Based in Parma, it is the world's largest pasta maker, and it has said more than a few billion plates are served using its pasta.
Italian brands, by founding year.Fiat: The name stands for Fabbrica Italiana Automobili Torino, and the Latin word fiat also means let it be done.
Italian brands, by founding year.Olivetti: Its red Valentine typewriter from 1969, designed by Ettore Sottsass, sits in New York's Museum of Modern Art.
Italian brands, by founding year.Vespa: The name means wasp in Italian, supposedly because of the buzz of the engine, and it starred in the film Roman Holiday.
Italian brands, by founding year.Luxottica: It owns Ray-Ban and Oakley, which makes it the world's largest eyewear company, and it merged with the lens maker Essilor.
Italian brands, by founding year.Benetton: It was founded by siblings in Treviso, in the Veneto region, and became known for colorful knitwear and provocative ad campaigns.
Italian brands, by founding year.Diesel: Founded by Renzo Rosso, the jeans brand has no connection to the engine's inventor, Rudolf Diesel, and the name was chosen to be international.

Tiny to huge: things inside you, by size.Width of the DNA helix: Stretched out, the DNA in one cell would be about two meters long, so it must be packed incredibly tightly into the nucleus.
Tiny to huge: things inside you, by size.Hemoglobin molecule: An iron-containing protein that carries up to four oxygen molecules each. Its iron is what makes blood red.
Tiny to huge: things inside you, by size.Ribosome: It builds proteins by reading messenger RNA, and is itself made mostly of RNA. A single cell can hold millions of them.
Tiny to huge: things inside you, by size.Flu virus: A flu virus carries eight separate RNA segments, which can reshuffle when two strains infect one cell, producing brand-new variants.
Tiny to huge: things inside you, by size.Mitochondrion: It has its own small DNA, inherited from the mother, a leftover from an ancient bacterium that moved into larger cells.
Tiny to huge: things inside you, by size.Platelet: Platelets are not full cells but fragments of giant cells in bone marrow. They lack a nucleus and clump to plug wounds.
Tiny to huge: things inside you, by size.Red blood cell: These cells have no nucleus and are shaped like squishy discs, so they can fold through the narrowest capillaries. They last about 120 days.
Tiny to huge: things inside you, by size.Neutrophil (white cell): The most common white blood cell and the first to arrive at an infection. Much of pus is dead neutrophils.
Tiny to huge: things inside you, by size.Egg cell: The largest human cell, just about visible to the naked eye as a speck. It carries only half the DNA needed to build a person.
Tiny to huge: things inside you, by size.Longest nerve cell: Motor neurons from the spinal cord to the toes are single cells with a fiber roughly a meter long, so one cell reaches your foot.

When these stars first went to the Olymp.Jim Thorpe: Thorpe, of the Sac and Fox Nation, won pentathlon and decathlon gold, then lost the medals over amateurism; they were later restored.
When these stars first went to the Olymp.Paavo Nurmi: Called the 'Flying Finn', he won nine golds across three Olympics and often ran with a stopwatch in his hand.
When these stars first went to the Olymp.Jesse Owens: His four golds in Berlin were a rebuke to the Nazi regime's racial ideology.
When these stars first went to the Olymp.Muhammad Ali (as Cassius Clay): At 18 he won light heavyweight gold in Rome, and was later given a replacement medal at Atlanta 1996.
When these stars first went to the Olymp.Mark Spitz: At the 1968 Games he won two relay golds and followed up with seven golds in 1972.
When these stars first went to the Olymp.Nadia Comaneci: At 14 she scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics; the scoreboard showed 1.00 because it could not show 10.00.
When these stars first went to the Olymp.Michael Jordan: He won gold in Los Angeles as a college player, and later returned with the 1992 Dream Team.
When these stars first went to the Olymp.Michael Phelps: He was the youngest US male swimmer in decades at 15, and he eventually won 23 Olympic golds.
When these stars first went to the Olymp.Usain Bolt: Eliminated in the heats at 17 in Athens, he returned to set world records in Beijing four years later.
When these stars first went to the Olymp.Simone Biles: Several gymnastics skills bear her name, and she won four golds in Rio.

Hop to it: jumpers by weight.Flea: A flea can leap dozens of times its own body length, powered by a springy protein called resilin rather than muscle alone.
Hop to it: jumpers by weight.Desert locust: A swarm can cover hundreds of square kilometers and each insect can eat roughly its own weight in plants every day.
Hop to it: jumpers by weight.Common frog: Common frogs hibernate through winter in pond mud or compost heaps, and spawn in huge clumps in early spring.
Hop to it: jumpers by weight.Jerboa: This desert rodent hops on long hind legs balanced by a tufted tail, a textbook case of evolving a kangaroo's trick independently.
Hop to it: jumpers by weight.Kangaroo rat: It can live its whole life without drinking, making water from the seeds it eats, and is neither a true rat nor a kangaroo.
Hop to it: jumpers by weight.European rabbit: The wild ancestor of every domestic rabbit breed; introduced to Australia in the 1800s, it became one of the country's worst pests.
Hop to it: jumpers by weight.Quokka: This small marsupial, found mainly on Rottnest Island, looks as if it is smiling, which made it a selfie celebrity.
Hop to it: jumpers by weight.Red-necked wallaby: Found in eastern Australia and Tasmania, it grazes at dusk and dawn, and its joey stays in the pouch for most of a year.
Hop to it: jumpers by weight.Springbok: South Africa's national animal does 'pronking', bouncing stiff-legged up to about two meters straight into the air.
Hop to it: jumpers by weight.Red kangaroo: The largest living marsupial can bound at over 50 km/h and clear a fence in a single leap.

House numbers of famous homes.The Dursleys' house: J.K. Rowling's hero was raised in the cupboard under the stairs at this Surrey address, where his aunt and uncle insisted they were perfectly normal.
House numbers of famous homes.UK Prime Minister's residence: The UK prime minister's official home looks modest from the street. Its famous black door has no outside keyhole or handle, so staff inside must open it.
House numbers of famous homes.Sirius Black's family home: The Black family's dark, hidden London mansion in the Harry Potter series is also the headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix.
House numbers of famous homes.Paddington's London home: Paddington lives with the Brown family at this fictional address, and the bear's love of marmalade sandwiches began in Peru.
House numbers of famous homes.Wallace & Gromit's house: This is the address of the cheese-loving inventor and his dog in Nick Park's clay animations, which began with A Grand Day Out.
House numbers of famous homes.SpongeBob's pineapple: Under the sea in Bikini Bottom, SpongeBob lives in a pineapple, next door to a rock for Patrick and an Easter Island head for Squidward.
House numbers of famous homes.Sherlock Holmes's lodgings: Arthur Conan Doyle's detective lived at this address, which did not exist when the stories were written. Baker Street's numbers were later extended.
House numbers of famous homes.The Simpsons' house: Homer, Marge and the kids live in a Springfield home, and the address is borrowed from a street in creator Matt Groening's hometown of Portland.
House numbers of famous homes.The Munsters' mansion: The Munster family's spooky Gothic house in the 1964 sitcom is home to Herman, Lily, Grandpa and a pet dragon named Spot living under the stairs.
House numbers of famous homes.The White House: Every US president since John Adams in 1800 has lived here. It has 132 rooms, and the address is often used to mean the presidency itself.

The life story of our Sun, in order.Collapsing gas cloud: The Sun formed about 4.6 billion years ago, and the leftover disk of material around it gave birth to the planets.
The life story of our Sun, in order.Hydrogen main sequence (now): Right now it fuses around 600 million tonnes of hydrogen every second, and has about five billion years of this left.
The life story of our Sun, in order.Subgiant: Once the core hydrogen is gone, it will slowly begin swelling, and warm Earth well beyond its comfort limit.
The life story of our Sun, in order.Red giant: The Sun will grow to hundreds of times its current width, swallowing Mercury and Venus, and probably Earth.
The life story of our Sun, in order.Helium flash: The core's helium will ignite within moments in a runaway burst, yet the star's thick outer layers hide the explosion.
The life story of our Sun, in order.Helium-burning core phase: A calmer period in which the Sun fuses helium into carbon and oxygen, lasting only about a hundred million years.
The life story of our Sun, in order.Asymptotic giant branch: The dying Sun will pulse and lose mass in strong winds, shedding much of its outer layers into space.
The life story of our Sun, in order.Planetary nebula: Despite the name it has nothing to do with planets. Early astronomers thought the glowing shell looked like a planet's disc.
The life story of our Sun, in order.White dwarf: The Sun's leftover core will be about Earth-sized, so dense that a teaspoon of it would weigh several tonnes.
The life story of our Sun, in order.Black dwarf (theoretical): None exist yet. A white dwarf needs far longer than the age of the universe to cool all the way.

Kitchen things by weight.Grain of rice: More than half the world's people rely on rice as a staple food.
Kitchen things by weight.Coffee bean: Coffee beans are seeds from a fruit called a cherry, and they are roasted to bring out flavour.
Kitchen things by weight.Sugar cube: Jakub Rad, a manager in Bohemia, made the first sugar cubes in 1843 after his wife cut her finger on a sugar cone.
Kitchen things by weight.Slice of bread: Sliced bread was first sold in 1928 in Missouri, after Otto Rohwedder invented a machine to slice it.
Kitchen things by weight.Large egg: A shell has thousands of tiny pores, so eggs can lose water and let oxygen in.
Kitchen things by weight.Banana: Bananas contain radioactive potassium, giving the banana equivalent dose as a joke unit of exposure.
Kitchen things by weight.Can of beans: The tin can was invented about 48 years before the can opener, and soldiers had to use bayonets.
Kitchen things by weight.Pineapple: It takes a pineapple about two years to grow, and each fruit is made from many tiny fused berries.
Kitchen things by weight.US bag of flour: Flour dust is explosive when suspended in air, and mills have suffered serious blasts.
Kitchen things by weight.Watermelon: It is about 92 percent water, and the fruit is related to cucumbers and pumpkins.

Brazilian states by area.Federal District: Brasília, the capital, was built from scratch in the late 1950s and inaugurated in 1960, designed by Lúcio Costa and Oscar Niemeyer.
Brazilian states by area.Sergipe: Brazil's smallest state by area, on the northeast coast, it still has a long Atlantic shoreline and the São Francisco River's mouth.
Brazilian states by area.Rio de Janeiro: Home to Christ the Redeemer and Carnival, its small size hides one of Brazil's best-known destinations.
Brazilian states by area.Pernambuco: Its capital, Recife, is nicknamed the 'Venice of Brazil' for its rivers and bridges.
Brazilian states by area.São Paulo: Though not the largest, it is Brazil's most populous state and produces roughly a third of the national economy.
Brazilian states by area.Goiás: It surrounds the Federal District of Brasília and is a major grower of soybeans and sugarcane.
Brazilian states by area.Minas Gerais: Its name means 'General Mines', from the 18th-century gold and diamond rush that built colonial towns like Ouro Preto.
Brazilian states by area.Mato Grosso: A leading producer of soybeans and cotton, it holds part of the Pantanal, the world's largest tropical wetland.
Brazilian states by area.Pará: Its capital Belém sits near the Amazon's mouth, and the Carajás mines supply much of Brazil's iron ore.
Brazilian states by area.Amazonas: Larger than most countries, it is mostly rainforest; its capital Manaus is a big city reachable mainly by river or air.

Star Wars on screen, by release.Star Wars (A New Hope): It was originally just 'Star Wars', and 'Episode IV: A New Hope' was added for a 1981 re-release.
Star Wars on screen, by release.The Empire Strikes Back: David Prowse spoke a different line on set so the 'I am your father' twist stayed secret.
Star Wars on screen, by release.Return of the Jedi: It was originally titled 'Revenge of the Jedi', changed because Jedi would not seek revenge.
Star Wars on screen, by release.The Phantom Menace: The first prequel arrived 16 years later and introduced Jar Jar Binks and Darth Maul.
Star Wars on screen, by release.The Clone Wars (film): This animated film launched the TV series and introduced Ahsoka Tano.
Star Wars on screen, by release.The Force Awakens: It became the highest-grossing film in North America at the time, with about $936 million.
Star Wars on screen, by release.Rogue One: It shows how the Death Star plans were stolen, leading into A New Hope.
Star Wars on screen, by release.Solo: A Star Wars Story: Directors Lord and Miller were replaced by Ron Howard mid-production, with Alden Ehrenreich as Han.
Star Wars on screen, by release.The Mandalorian: The first live-action Star Wars TV series introduced Grogu, widely known as 'Baby Yoda'.
Star Wars on screen, by release.Andor: A spy-thriller prequel to Rogue One, praised for its gritty political drama.

The Twelve Imams of Shia Islam, in order.Ali: The first Imam, Ali, was the Prophet Muhammad's cousin and son-in-law, and Shia Muslims regard him as his rightful successor.
The Twelve Imams of Shia Islam, in order.Hasan: The Prophet's grandson Hasan agreed to a peace treaty with Muawiya, and is revered as the second Imam.
The Twelve Imams of Shia Islam, in order.Husayn: Killed at Karbala in 680, his martyrdom is mourned each year on Ashura, with processions and passion plays.
The Twelve Imams of Shia Islam, in order.Zayn al-Abidin: Known as 'the Ornament of the Worshippers', he survived Karbala and is remembered for his book of prayers, the Sahifa Sajjadiyya.
The Twelve Imams of Shia Islam, in order.Muhammad al-Baqir: His title 'al-Baqir' means 'the one who splits knowledge open', a tribute to his deep learning.
The Twelve Imams of Shia Islam, in order.Ja'far al-Sadiq: A scholar who taught many students, he gave his name to the Ja'fari school of Shia jurisprudence.
The Twelve Imams of Shia Islam, in order.Musa al-Kazim: He spent years in prison under the Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid, and his title al-Kazim means 'the one who restrains anger'.
The Twelve Imams of Shia Islam, in order.Ali al-Rida: The only Imam buried in Iran, he rests at Mashhad, one of the world's great pilgrimage cities.
The Twelve Imams of Shia Islam, in order.Hasan al-Askari: He was the father of the twelfth Imam, and lived under tight surveillance in the garrison city of Samarra.
The Twelve Imams of Shia Islam, in order.Muhammad al-Mahdi: Twelvers believe he went into hiding, called occultation, and remains alive, to return as a savior, the Mahdi.

How old were these characters?.Heidi, arriving in the Alps: Johanna Spyri's orphan is sent to live with her grandfather, and the book has sold tens of millions worldwide.
How old were these characters?.Alice, in Looking-Glass: Lewis Carroll's sequel has the girl enter a chess-themed world, where she meets Tweedledum and Tweedledee, and Jabberwocky.
How old were these characters?.Harry, starting Hogwarts: The boy wizard starts at Hogwarts at 11, after getting his letter, delivered by owl.
How old were these characters?.Juliet: Shakespeare's heroine is not quite 14, and her tragedy unfolds in just a few days.
How old were these characters?.Katniss, at the Reaping: Suzanne Collins' heroine volunteers in her sister's place at the Reaping, and the games televised from Panem's Capitol.
How old were these characters?.Frodo, leaving the Shire: Frodo is 50 when he leaves the Shire, because the Ring slowed his aging, and 33 when he inherited it.
How old were these characters?.Bilbo, at his farewell party: Bilbo's 111th birthday is celebrated with a huge party, and he vanishes, using the Ring, in front of everyone.
How old were these characters?.Yoda, at his death: The Jedi master Yoda lived 900 years, and he died peacefully in Return of the Jedi, and vanished into the Force.
How old were these characters?.Noah, at his death: The biblical Noah is said to have lived 950 years, and he built an ark to survive the flood.
How old were these characters?.Methuselah, at his death: The longest-lived person in the Bible, he lived 969 years, and his name is now a byword for great age.

Space telescopes by launch year.Uhuru (X-ray): Launched from Kenya, its name means "freedom" in Swahili, and it was the first satellite dedicated to mapping X-ray sources.
Space telescopes by launch year.IRAS: It was the first telescope to survey the whole sky in infrared, and it found dust rings around nearby stars including Vega.
Space telescopes by launch year.Hubble: After launch its mirror turned out to be slightly misshapen, and astronauts fitted corrective optics in 1993.
Space telescopes by launch year.Chandra: Named for astrophysicist Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar, it sees X-rays from black holes and exploded stars that never reach the ground.
Space telescopes by launch year.Spitzer: This infrared observatory trailed behind Earth in orbit and helped discover the seven planets of the TRAPPIST-1 system.
Space telescopes by launch year.Kepler: By watching stars dim as planets passed in front, it showed that planets are more common than stars in our galaxy.
Space telescopes by launch year.Gaia: This European mission is charting the positions and motions of well over a billion stars to build a 3D map of our galaxy.
Space telescopes by launch year.TESS: It scans nearly the whole sky for planets orbiting bright, nearby stars, picking up where Kepler left off.
Space telescopes by launch year.James Webb: Its 6.5 m gold-coated mirror unfolded in space, and it sits about 1.5 million km from Earth, shielded from the Sun by a tennis-court sized sunshield.
Space telescopes by launch year.Euclid: This European telescope aims to chart the shape of the dark universe by observing billions of galaxies.

When these bizarre events happened.Dancing Plague of Strasbourg: Hundreds of people in this French city danced for days without rest, and some reportedly died of exhaustion.
When these bizarre events happened.Tulip mania crash: At the peak of the craze, a single rare tulip bulb sold for the price of a house, before prices collapsed.
When these bizarre events happened.War of Jenkins' Ear begins: Britain went to war with Spain after a captain's severed ear was shown to Parliament.
When these bizarre events happened.London Beer Flood: A brewery vat burst in London, flooding streets with about 1.4 million liters of beer and killing eight people.
When these bizarre events happened.Great Moon Hoax: A New York newspaper published fake reports of bat-winged people living on the Moon, and readers believed them.
When these bizarre events happened.Great Stink of London: The Thames reeked so much that Parliament hung curtains soaked in lime, which pushed it to fund new sewers.
When these bizarre events happened.Kentucky meat shower: Chunks of meat fell from a clear sky in Kentucky, and a likely explanation is that vultures vomited it.
When these bizarre events happened.Boston Molasses Flood: A storage tank burst and a wave of syrup rushed through the Boston streets, killing 21 people.
When these bizarre events happened.Great Emu War: Australia sent soldiers with machine guns to fight emus damaging wheat crops, and the birds largely won.
When these bizarre events happened.War of the Worlds radio panic: Orson Welles's radio drama about a Martian invasion was said to have panicked listeners, though historians think the panic was exaggerated.

When these cartoon characters debuted.Felix the Cat: Felix became a movie star in the silent era, and he was the first cartoon character to have merchandise and be an international sensation.
When these cartoon characters debuted.Mickey Mouse: Mickey first appeared in Steamboat Willie, one of the first cartoons with synchronized sound, and Walt Disney originally voiced him himself.
When these cartoon characters debuted.Betty Boop: Betty was originally drawn as a French poodle with floppy ears before becoming a human flapper, and she was a 1930s icon.
When these cartoon characters debuted.Donald Duck: Donald first appeared in The Wise Little Hen, and Clarence Nash voiced him for decades with his famously garbled quack.
When these cartoon characters debuted.Bugs Bunny: Bugs first appeared in A Wild Hare in 1940, and his catchphrase 'Eh, what's up, Doc?' was born in that cartoon.
When these cartoon characters debuted.Road Runner: This coyote-chasing bird's 'beep beep' was inspired by director Chuck Jones's desire to parody chase cartoons, and the Acme gadgets always backfire.
When these cartoon characters debuted.Scooby-Doo: This Great Dane premiered in 1969 and, famously, was designed after an actual breed expert's advice, with his mystery-solving gang.
When these cartoon characters debuted.Garfield: Jim Davis named him after his grandfather James Garfield Davis, and this lasagna-loving cat became the world's most syndicated comic strip.
When these cartoon characters debuted.Pikachu: Created for the Pokémon games, Pikachu was designed to be cute, and it became the franchise's mascot ahead of the starter trio.
When these cartoon characters debuted.SpongeBob SquarePants: Stephen Hillenburg, a marine biology teacher, created this sea sponge; the show became Nickelodeon's longest-running cartoon.

Recommended daily intake for an adult ma.Vitamin B12: Found almost only in animal foods, so vegans need supplements or fortified products.
Recommended daily intake for an adult ma.Vitamin D: Skin makes it from sunlight; 15 micrograms equals 600 international units.
Recommended daily intake for an adult ma.Folate: The name comes from foliage, as in spinach, and it is vital in early pregnancy to prevent neural tube defects.
Recommended daily intake for an adult ma.Iron: Women need more, about 18 mg, since they lose iron monthly; meat iron is absorbed better than plant iron.
Recommended daily intake for an adult ma.Zinc: Oysters are by far the richest source of this mineral, which supports immunity.
Recommended daily intake for an adult ma.Vitamin C: One orange has about 70 mg; humans, guinea pigs and some bats cannot make their own.
Recommended daily intake for an adult ma.Magnesium: Needed for hundreds of enzyme reactions, it is found in nuts, seeds and leafy greens.
Recommended daily intake for an adult ma.Calcium: About 99 percent of the body's calcium is stored in bones and teeth.
Recommended daily intake for an adult ma.Sodium (upper limit): 2,300 mg of sodium is about one teaspoon of table salt, a limit most people exceed.
Recommended daily intake for an adult ma.Potassium: Bananas are famous for it, but beans, potatoes and spinach contain more.

When these substances were isolated or m.Morphine: Friedrich Sertürner isolated morphine from opium, and named it after Morpheus, the Greek god of dreams.
When these substances were isolated or m.Caffeine: Caffeine was isolated by Friedlieb Runge at the suggestion of Goethe, and it's the world's most-used stimulant.
When these substances were isolated or m.Nicotine: Nicotine was isolated from tobacco, and it's named after Jean Nicot, who brought tobacco to France.
When these substances were isolated or m.Cocaine: Cocaine was isolated from coca leaves, and it was once an ingredient in tonics and early Coca-Cola.
When these substances were isolated or m.Amphetamine: Amphetamine was first synthesized in Berlin, and it wasn't used as a medicine until the 1930s.
When these substances were isolated or m.Methamphetamine: Methamphetamine was synthesized in Japan by Nagai Nagayoshi, and it was used by soldiers in World War II.
When these substances were isolated or m.MDMA: MDMA was made by Merck, and it was patented as an intermediate, and was not used by humans until later.
When these substances were isolated or m.LSD: Albert Hofmann first made LSD in Basel, and he discovered its effects when he accidentally absorbed some, and the bicycle day followed.
When these substances were isolated or m.Psilocybin: Psilocybin was isolated by Albert Hofmann from magic mushrooms, and it's being studied for depression.
When these substances were isolated or m.Ketamine: Ketamine was developed as an anesthetic, and it's now also used as a fast-acting treatment for depression.

Sci-fi TV series premieres.The Twilight Zone: The Twilight Zone was created by Rod Serling, and its twist endings influenced decades of TV.
Sci-fi TV series premieres.The Outer Limits: The Outer Limits opened with the line We control the horizontal, and it was known for monsters and moral fables.
Sci-fi TV series premieres.Battlestar Galactica (orig.): Battlestar Galactica was a Star Wars-era space epic, and it was later rebooted in 2004 to wide acclaim.
Sci-fi TV series premieres.The X-Files: The X-Files followed agents Mulder and Scully, and its tagline The Truth Is Out There became iconic.
Sci-fi TV series premieres.Stargate SG-1: Stargate SG-1 ran for ten seasons, and it was one of the longest-running American sci-fi shows.
Sci-fi TV series premieres.Firefly: Firefly was canceled after 14 episodes, but fan campaigns led to the film Serenity.
Sci-fi TV series premieres.Fringe: Fringe was a J.J. Abrams show about parallel universes, and it's been recognized for its inventive plots.
Sci-fi TV series premieres.Black Mirror: Black Mirror was created by Charlie Brooker, and its episodes are standalone stories about technology gone wrong.
Sci-fi TV series premieres.Westworld: Westworld was based on a 1973 film by Michael Crichton, and it features androids in a theme park.
Sci-fi TV series premieres.Severance: Severance follows workers whose memories are surgically separated between work and home, and it's set at Lumon Industries.

Things that spin, by revolutions per min.Clock's hour hand: The hour hand creeps just half a degree per minute, easy to see over an hour but never in a moment.
Things that spin, by revolutions per min.Clock's minute hand: It sweeps six degrees every minute, and in some old clocks it lagged slightly between ticks.
Things that spin, by revolutions per min.Clock's second hand: Quartz clocks tick once a second, while mechanical watches beat several times a second, giving a smoother sweep.
Things that spin, by revolutions per min.LP vinyl record: Columbia introduced the LP in 1948, and one side held about 20 to 25 minutes of music.
Things that spin, by revolutions per min.Vinyl single: RCA Victor launched the 45 in 1949, and its wide center hole suited jukebox changers.
Things that spin, by revolutions per min.Old shellac record: Standard for shellac discs for decades, the 78 was made from a resin secreted by the lac insect.
Things that spin, by revolutions per min.Car engine at idle: Engine computers hold idle speed steady, even as the air conditioner or lights pull more power.
Things that spin, by revolutions per min.Desktop hard drive: Its heads hover on a cushion of air just nanometres above the platter.
Things that spin, by revolutions per min.F1 engine at max: Rules have capped Formula 1 engines at 15,000 rpm since 2014, down from 18,000 in the V8 era.
Things that spin, by revolutions per min.Dental drill: Air-driven handpieces spin faster than a jet engine's turbine, which is why they emit that high whine.

Milestones in physics, chemistry and mat.Euclid's Elements: A single geometry textbook shaped teaching for about 2,000 years, one of the most reprinted books ever.
Milestones in physics, chemistry and mat.Galileo's telescope: He improved a Dutch spyglass, then spotted Jupiter's four big moons in 1610.
Milestones in physics, chemistry and mat.Newton's Principia: Edmond Halley paid for its printing, and it laid out the laws of motion and universal gravitation.
Milestones in physics, chemistry and mat.Mendeleev's periodic table: His gaps for undiscovered elements correctly predicted gallium, germanium and scandium.
Milestones in physics, chemistry and mat.Discovery of X-rays: Röntgen's first X-ray image was of his wife's hand, with her ring showing, and he won the first Nobel Prize in Physics.
Milestones in physics, chemistry and mat.Special relativity: Einstein produced it as a patent clerk in Bern, during his 1905 'miracle year'.
Milestones in physics, chemistry and mat.First nuclear reactor: Chicago Pile-1 was built by Enrico Fermi under the stands of a university stadium.
Milestones in physics, chemistry and mat.The transistor: Bardeen, Brattain and Shockley won a Nobel for it, and modern chips contain billions.
Milestones in physics, chemistry and mat.Fermat's Last Theorem proved: Andrew Wiles solved it after about 350 years, when Fermat's margin note had left it unproven.
Milestones in physics, chemistry and mat.Higgs boson found: The Large Hadron Collider found it at CERN, and Higgs and Englert shared the 2013 Nobel Prize.

Horror films, by release year.Nosferatu: An unauthorized Dracula adaptation, it nearly got destroyed after Bram Stoker's widow sued, yet it survived and inspired generations of vampire movies.
Horror films, by release year.Frankenstein: Boris Karloff's flat-headed monster, created with makeup by Jack Pierce, became a defining image of Hollywood horror.
Horror films, by release year.Psycho: Hitchcock bought up copies of the novel to protect its twist and refused to let audiences in once the film started.
Horror films, by release year.Night of the Living Dead: George Romero's low-budget film essentially created the modern zombie movie, and was made for around 100,000 dollars.
Horror films, by release year.The Exorcist: The film was so frightening that some audience members reportedly fainted, and it was the first horror film nominated for Best Picture.
Horror films, by release year.Halloween: John Carpenter made it on a tiny budget and composed its famous piano theme himself, and it helped define the slasher genre.
Horror films, by release year.Friday the 13th: Made to cash in on Halloween's success, it started a long franchise, though Jason wasn't the killer in the first film.
Horror films, by release year.A Nightmare on Elm Street: Wes Craven's film introduced Freddy Krueger, a killer who attacks in dreams, and it helped save a struggling New Line Cinema.
Horror films, by release year.Scream: Written as a knowing take on slasher films, it revived the genre by having characters who've seen all the horror movies.
Horror films, by release year.Get Out: Jordan Peele's directorial debut won an Oscar for Best Original Screenplay, using horror to explore race in America.

New Year's Eve, in sound and light.Burns sends Auld Lang Syne: Robert Burns sent the poem to a collector of Scottish songs, saying he'd written it down from an old man's singing.
New Year's Eve, in sound and light.Times Square ball drop: The first drop was in 1907 after the New York Times, which owned a tower there, banned fireworks; the ball has been replaced many times.
New Year's Eve, in sound and light.Lombardo's radio broadcast: Bandleader Guy Lombardo and the Royal Canadians made Auld Lang Syne their New Year's trademark, broadcasting it across North America for decades.
New Year's Eve, in sound and light.Rockin' Eve debuts: Dick Clark's New Year's special, created as a rival to Lombardo's, brought pop acts to Times Square and helped define countdown television.
New Year's Eve, in sound and light.ABBA's Happy New Year: The bittersweet song was written by Benny and Björn, and it is about morning-after resolutions rather than celebration.
New Year's Eve, in sound and light.Prince's 1999: Prince's party anthem about the end of the millennium returned to the charts at the end of the actual year 1999.
New Year's Eve, in sound and light.U2's New Year's Day: Despite its title, the song was inspired by Poland's Solidarity movement and Lech Wałęsa, not holiday celebrations.
New Year's Eve, in sound and light.Y2K midnight: Fears about a computer bug in two-digit years largely fizzled out after billions were spent on fixing systems.
New Year's Eve, in sound and light.Burj Khalifa fireworks: Dubai's 828-meter tower, the tallest building in the world, hosts a spectacular light and fireworks show to ring in the year.
New Year's Eve, in sound and light.Taylor Swift's New Year's Day: The quiet piano ballad closing her album Reputation is about staying with someone through the messy aftermath of a party.
